notes: Fiscal-year labeling: schema years 2023-2025 correspond to SWK fiscal years ended Dec. 30, 2023; Dec. 28, 2024; and Jan. 3, 2026 respectively. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))

EBIT definition: computed from continuing-operations earnings before income taxes plus interest expense minus interest income (equivalent to EBITDA - D&A under the disclosed EBITDA/D&A reconciliation). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))

NWC definition: computed as (Total current assets - cash and cash equivalents) - (Total current liabilities - short-term borrowings - current maturities of long-term debt). Includes 'current assets/liabilities held for sale' because they are presented within current balance sheet totals. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))

NOL balance: taken from disclosure of U.S. ($1.6B) and foreign ($3.8B) net operating loss carryforwards available to reduce future tax obligations; utilization rate not disclosed, so set to null. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))

Comps: EV/NTM revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, and P/E NTM were not populated because forward-multiple granularity for this peer set was not reliably retrievable within this run; tickers are provided for later enrichment.

WACC: sourced from a third-party market-data calculation (StockAnalysis). If you require a fully model-built WACC (risk-free + beta*ERP + cost of debt*after-tax using target leverage), you should override wacc in your pipeline.

catalysts: Portfolio/divestiture execution (including CAM) and resulting balance-sheet improvement that supports further deleveraging. ([newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com](https://newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com/2026-02-04-Stanley-Black-Decker-Reports-4Q-and-Full-Year-2025-Results))

Sustained EBIT margin expansion as supply-chain transformation and productivity savings translate through the P&L. ([newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com](https://newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com/2026-02-04-Stanley-Black-Decker-Reports-4Q-and-Full-Year-2025-Results))
Reduction in tariff-driven volume/promotional headwinds during 2H 2026, enabling steadier demand and mix.
company_overview: Stanley Black & Decker operates as a global diversified industrial company with two reportable segments: Tools & Outdoor and Engineered Fastening. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))

Key brand portfolio includes DEWALT®, STANLEY®, BLACK+DECKER®, and CRAFTSMAN® (Tools & Outdoor), alongside engineered fastening components (Engineered Fastening). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))
current_context: In its Feb. 4, 2026 results release, management guided 2026 GAAP EPS of $3.15 to $4.35 and adjusted EPS of $4.90 to $5.70 (midpoints: +42% GAAP and +13% adjusted). ([newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com](https://newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com/2026-02-04-Stanley-Black-Decker-Reports-4Q-and-Full-Year-2025-Results))

The company also targeted 2026 free cash flow of $700M to $900M (midpoint: +16%), reflecting ongoing working-capital improvements and cash-flow focus. ([newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com](https://newsroom.stanleyblackanddecker.com/2026-02-04-Stanley-Black-Decker-Reports-4Q-and-Full-Year-2025-Results))

The update emphasized tariff landscape impacts early in 2026 and execution on supply-chain/productivity actions to support margin and cash generation. ([fool.com](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/02/04/stanley-black-decker-swk-earnings-transcript/?utm_source=openai))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes revenue stabilizes after 2023-2025 declines and grows modestly from 2026 onward, consistent with management’s focus on operational excellence and demand support initiatives. ([stanleyblackanddecker.com](https://www.stanleyblackanddecker.com/stanley-black-decker-reports-2q-2025-results?utm_source=openai))

EBIT margin expansion is driven by cost actions and supply-chain transformation benefits, moving from mid-single-digit EBIT margin toward the base-case target by 2030. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))
D&A, capex intensity, and NWC intensity are modeled within/near recent historical ranges, supporting a relatively steady reinvestment profile and cash conversion.
Terminal value is underpinned by a conservative Gordon-growth terminal framework rather than an aggressive exit multiple.
key_risks: Tariff and end-market demand volatility could pressure volume and gross margin, slowing EBIT margin recovery versus base case.

Working-capital performance may deteriorate if inventory/order timing or receivables terms worsen (dragging free cash flow). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093556/000120677426000122/swk4498821-ars.pdf))
Execution risk around supply-chain transformation and footprint actions could delay margin improvement and raise costs.
